key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within seconds. LOCATION: GENERALIZED or focal. DURATION: Lasts seconds to minutes. CHARACTER: INVOLUNTARY movements, jerking, convulsions. AGGRAVATING: STRESS, sleep deprivation, medication non-compliance. RELIEVING: ANTICONVULSANTS, supportive care. TIMING: Sudden onset, lasts seconds to minutes. SEVERITY: 8-10/10 during episode, then resolves. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: LOSS OF CONSCIOUSNESS, jerking movements, tongue biting, incontinence, postictal confusion. KEY POSITIVES: Involuntary movements, loss of consciousness, postictal confusion, tongue biting. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no photophobia.

red_flags: Seizure lasting >5 minutes - status epilepticus, call 911
Multiple seizures without regaining consciousness - status epilepticus, call 911
Seizure with severe head injury - possible traumatic brain injury, call 911
Seizure with signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Seizure with severe hypertension - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
